messages:
Joel: Quick sync — I sketched a long-term roadmap for regional routing + multi-tenant isolation. Link: https://docs.internal/redwood/arch/region-routing-proposal (short read). Looking for: launch criteria, customer-driven priorities, and a minimal migration path.
Anya: skimmed it — nice. I think we should be explicit about a "phased neutral-route" approach rather than immediate hard isolation. avoids breaking customers.
Mike: agree with phased. Also we need a concrete canary + fallback policy spelled out (how do we fallback to global model without violating residency?).
Sam: note on implementation: per-tenant KV cache + hot-shard affinity is the expensive bit. Memory multiplies by tenant slices. rough spike: +30% RAM for soft-isolation.
Tara: FYI: several pilot customers asked for an "isolation window" SLA. they want a committed timeline for Dedicated or VPC options. How soon can we promise something?
Joel: high-level phases I proposed:
- Phase 0: Guardrails & routing policy DSL (no tenant isolation). config + telemetry + policy evaluation.
- Phase 1: Soft slices — steering/affinity, prefix caching per-slice, graceful eviction (no dedicated infra).
- Phase 2: Tenant-banded capacity — logical isolation, routable to reserved pools (Dedicated opt-in).
- Phase 3: Hard isolation (private deployment + strict egress/residency).
Anya: for each phase we should list launch gates. e.g. Phase1 gate = canary 48h, telemetry coverage 95% for routing decisions, rollback <10min.
Devin: propose prioritization formula: score = 2*customer_impact + 3*security_requirements - 0.5*engineering_effort + 1*cost_delta. keeps safety weighted.
Mike: gating specifics:
- Canary: 1% traffic -> 5% -> 20% over 48–72h windows
- Instrumentation: trace sampling + per-tenant p50/p95/p99 latency + cold-kv miss rate
- Fallbacks: policy-based auto-fallback to model-variant in same region or global fallback lane with trace flag
Sam: small config example for routing policy we discussed:
```
policy:
  prefer: regional
  fallbacks: [reserved_pool, global]
  evict_after: 30m
```
Tara: customers to involve in pilot: Acme, BetaHealth, Atlas — all asked for some form of regional isolation. I'll coordinate PI invites.
Joel: launch criteria checklist (working draft):
- SLA target defined for each phase (latency & availability)
- Telemetry coverage: tracing + token-level cost breakdown enabled
- Migration plan + rollback runbook + escalation path
- Legal/KMS signoff for residency where needed
- Pricing/packaging decision for Dedicated opt-in
Anya: dependencies callout: model-aware routing hooks (need model metadata service), cross-region bandwidth accounting, KMS integration for Private.
Mike: ops checklist: preflight tests (synthetic):
- regional failover test
- prefix cache cold-start test
- eviction and rehydration under load
ops-bot: Scheduled: infra-spike/region-routing (2025-08-12) added to eng-infra board :gear:
Sam: rough engineering sizing: Phase0: 5 SP, Phase1: 25 SP (spike + infra changes), Phase2: 45 SP (capacity + networking), Phase3: 30 SP (packaging + compliance).
Devin: can we map these to quarters? Phase0 Q3, Phase1 Q4, Phase2 Q1 next year, Phase3 Q2 next year? depends on resourcing.
Joel: tentative roadmap — sounds reasonable. Action items:
1) Anya + Sam: produce a 2-week infra spike to validate kv-memory impact + canary plumbing
2) Mike: draft canary + rollback runbook (include tracing playbook)
3) Tara: lock pilot customers and capture their acceptance criteria
4) Devin: apply prioritization formula to outstanding customer asks and return a ranked list by next Wed
5) Joel: coordinate legal/KMS checklist and price/packaging stub
Anya: I'll start a doc for Phase1 runbook and tag owners.
Tara: will set a pilot kickoff with Acme for next Tue.
Mike: will mock a failover simulation by EOD Friday.
Sam: I'll start the infra spike branch and post rough numbers in the doc.
Devin: will share the scored list Wed AM.
Joel: perfect. If anyone sees a missing launch gate, call it out here. Otherwise I'll sync with PMs and put a milestone in roadmap. :thumbsup:
Anya: one ask — add a cost-per-token delta estimate per phase so sales can model price changes.
Sam: noted. I'll include perf/cost delta in the spike report.
Tara: sounds good. thanks all.
Joel: thanks — closing this thread.
